assumptions: Average time per generated image is treated as an inference-efficiency metric, not as hardware or on-device evidence.

verdicts.reason: The cited abstract span directly frames spatial-composition and object-counting control as weaknesses of text-to-image diffusion models.
The cited span explicitly presents MAC as training-free and says it eliminates additional modules and fine-tuning.
The cited span directly describes using text-visual cross-attention maps to quantify layout inconsistency and losses to optimize latent features during reverse diffusion.
The cited experimental setup names SD 1.5 as the base model and SD-XL and GLIGEN for ablation study.
The cited evaluation span lists exactly A&E, BoxDiff, Layout-Guidance, A&R, R&B, and LoCo as comparison methods.
The cited DrawBench result gives R&B as the best baseline and reports the same precision, recall, and F1 improvements.

The source supports best overall HRS performance and the three improvement values, but the cited span does not identify all compared methods as the baseline for those percentages; saying the improvements are over the compared methods blurs the comparison baseline.
The cited span directly reports more than double average generation time for R&B versus MAC with comparable performance; it remains a software timing result with no named physical device.
The cited ablation span directly states that marginal-attention loss resolves overlap but may cause attention vanishing.
The cited span states that attention vanishing does not occur with only one bounding box per phrase, supporting the stated multi-box condition.
The cited ablation span reports that regularization addresses attention vanishing and produces exactly one object per bounding box in Figure 5(c).
